note: F5-6000J2836G16GX2-TZ5NR: F5 is DDR5 (F4 DDR4), then the MT/s, then a letter and the timings.

CMK32GX5M2B6000C30: family (CMK Vengeance, CMH Vengeance RGB, CMT Dominator, CMSX SODIMM, CMW/CMD DDR4), kit capacity, GX5 = DDR5, M2 = two modules, revision letter, MT/s, then C for the CAS or Z on the AMD EXPO kits.
KF560C36BBEK2-32: KF5 is DDR5, 60 = 6000 MT/s, C36 = CAS. DDR4 (KF4) is left out because 26 means 2666 there, not 2600.
KVR48U40BS8-16: 48 = 4800 MT/s, U = unbuffered DDR5, 40 = CAS. JEDEC parts with no profile to enable: the rated speed is the JEDEC speed.
CP2K16G60C36U5B: Crucial Pro carries XMP/EXPO profiles; kit capacity, 60 = 6000 MT/s, CAS, U5 = DDR5 UDIMM (S5 SODIMM).

CT16G56C46U5: plain Crucial DDR5 is a JEDEC part (56 = 5600 MT/s, CAS 46) with no XMP/EXPO profile; a platform that runs it slower is not a setting the user can change. DDR4 Crucial parts use another layout and are left out.
TEAMGROUP-UD5-6000: what the SPD (and so WMI) reports for T-Force kits; UD5 is DDR5 UDIMM (UD4 DDR4), then the MT/s. The retail SKU (FF3D532G6000HC38ADC01) never reaches the part-number field.
PVV532G6000C36K (Venom), PVVR5 (Venom RGB), PVE5 (Elite 5): family letters, 5 = DDR5, kit capacity, MT/s, CAS. Parts that shorten the speed to two digits (PVX532G80C38K) are not decoded.
AX5U6000C3016G-DCLABK (XPG Lancer), AX4U360016G18I-DB50 (XPG DDR4): AX, DDR generation, U = UDIMM, then the MT/s.
AD5U480016G-B (ADATA Premier): the same layout as XPG, but a JEDEC module with no profile.

M425R1GB4BB0-CQK0D (the first laptop, an ASUS GA402RJ: two DDR5-4800 SO-DIMMs): M425 is a DDR5 SO-DIMM (M323 UDIMM, M321 RDIMM), R the DDR5 generation, 1GB4 the density, BB0 the die revision, then -C and the speed grade: QK is 4800B, WM is 5600B. JEDEC modules with no profile; a grade not listed here is unknown, never guessed.
MTC8C1084S1SC48BA1: MTC is a DDR5 module, then the organisation, S1 single rank, S = SO-DIMM (U = UDIMM), C48 = 4800 MT/s (C56 = 5600). Laptop and OEM desktop JEDEC modules with no profile.
